chunk.text: AI-Powered Customer Support Platform
Business Proposal and Investment Case

Prepared for: Executive Leadership Team
Test document for Blind Spot AI multimodal analysis, RAG, and multi-agent debate
1. Executive Summary

This proposal recommends deploying an AI-powered customer support platform across the company. The platform would classify incoming tickets, answer routine questions, translate customer messages, and escalate complex cases to human agents.

Management expects the platform to reduce annual support costs by approximately 40% while improving customer satisfaction. The proposal assumes that approximately 70% of incoming tickets can eventually be resolved without human intervention.

The business case is attractive, but several assumptions require validation before full deployment. The proposal does not yet include a completed privacy impact assessment, an independent security review, or a controlled customer pilot.
2. Current Problem

The customer support organization currently handles approximately 80,000 tickets per month. Average first-response time is eight hours, and customer satisfaction is reported at 72%. Management believes that slow response times are a major contributor to customer dissatisfaction.
Support leaders also report that a substantial portion of tickets involve repetitive questions about billing, account access, shipping status, and product documentation.
3. Proposed Solution

The proposed platform will combine a customer-facing AI assistant with automated ticket classification and a human escalation workflow. The system will use company documentation and approved support knowledge as retrieval sources.
Automated classification and routing of incoming support tickets.
AI-generated responses for routine questions.
Human escalation for high-risk, sensitive, or low-confidence cases.
Multilingual support for major customer languages.
Analytics dashboard covering resolution rate, response time, and escalation volume.
4. Financial Analysis
The following figures are management estimates. They have not yet been independently audited.

The target model implies substantial productivity gains. However, the proposal does not clearly separate gross labor savings from net savings after infrastructure, monitoring, model usage, security, training, and ongoing maintenance costs.
5. Key Assumptions
At least 70% of tickets can be resolved automatically after deployment.
AI answer accuracy will remain above 95% under normal production conditions.
Customers will generally prefer AI-assisted support when response times are shorter.
Implementation can be completed by a three-engineer core team within the proposed schedule.
Existing support documentation is sufficiently accurate and complete for retrieval.
The training and knowledge data contains no significant demographic or language bias.
Human agents can effectively review escalated conversations without creating a new operational bottleneck.
6. Risk Assessment
7. Security and Privacy Considerations

Customer conversations may contain names, addresses, account information, purchase history, and other sensitive business data. The platform should minimize data retention, restrict access by role, encrypt data in transit and at rest, and maintain audit logs.

Before production launch, the company should define retention periods, incident-response procedures, vendor responsibilities, and controls for prompt injection or malicious content embedded in customer messages.
8. Ethics and Workforce Impact

Automation may reduce repetitive work, but it could also change the responsibilities of support staff. A responsible deployment should measure whether AI performance differs across languages, customer groups, and issue categories. Customers should have a clear path to human assistance.
9. Implementation Timeline
10. Measurement Plan
First-response time and resolution time.
AI resolution rate and human escalation rate.
Customer satisfaction compared with a baseline control group.
Accuracy and groundedness of AI answers.
Security incidents and privacy-related events.
Performance by language, issue type, and customer segment.
Net support cost after all AI operating expenses.
11. Questions Requiring Executive Review
Is the 40% cost reduction supported by a complete total-cost-of-ownership model?
What evidence supports the 70% automated resolution target?
How will hallucinations and unsupported claims be detected before answers reach customers?
Which customer data may be sent to external AI services, and under what contractual controls?
What happens when the AI system is unavailable or produces low-confidence answers?
How will employees and customers appeal or correct an incorrect AI decision?
What independent security and privacy testing must be completed before launch?
12. Recommendation

Proceed with a controlled pilot rather than immediate full deployment. The expected operational benefits are potentially significant, but the financial, security, privacy, accuracy, and workforce assumptions should be validated using real customer-support data before the business commits to the full target case.
